title: The First Ripple
scene: He arrives. Relief gives way to distance.

paragraphs: Mukund knocked once and let himself in when she called.
He was still wearing his coat. He had found a parking space farther down the block than he wanted, and on the walk back he had rehearsed three different questions.
Aarna was on the floor with a painting against her knees.
"Hey."
She looked up, then down again.
He put his bag beside the door and crouched next to her. "Show me what they said."
While he read the message, she leaned against his shoulder. He lowered one knee to the floor.
Funding. No replacement date. He scrolled down, although there was nothing below the signature.
"You don't have to say anything yet," she said.
He rested his hand against her back.
"We'll find another way."
She nodded against his coat.
"Two weeks is still time. The work's ready."
She lifted her head and took the phone back.
"Remember that upstairs room? The photography thing we went to?"
"I remember."
"They rent it out."
He stood to get his laptop. There was a scrap of paper on the wall with a cross drawn on it. The hammer was on a chair. He moved it onto the windowsill before sitting down.
For a minute, she had thought she might finally cry.
His coat had brought the cold in with him. She could feel it leaving the fabric beneath her cheek. He was here; she did not have to work out what to say first.
Now he was at the table.
"They aren't answering. I'll send a message."
She watched him type. He took his coat off without looking away from the screen and hung it over the back of the chair.
"Mukund."
"One second."
He finished the message.
"I don't want to call anyone."
"You don't have to. I'll do it."
"That's not what I meant."
He closed one tab. Three remained open.
She ran her thumb along the frame. "Room Enough is the one I was going to..."
"What?"
He was reading the dimensions another venue wanted.
"Nothing."
"This one's too small anyway."
She looked at the pale doorway. The coat-hook marks. There was a little chip in the frame that she had meant to cover before the photograph.
"Could we not?"
He took his hands off the keyboard.
His phone showed two missed calls from work. He turned it face down beside the laptop.
"I'm only looking."
"I know."
"You asked me to come."
She went still.
"Yes," she said. "I did."
He rubbed the place on his knee where the floor had pressed through his trousers. He could hear traffic moving again outside, a bus pulling away from the corner.
The laptop dimmed. He touched the trackpad and the room brightened.
Aarna glanced at the screen, then at the empty chair between them.
He moved his hand away.
"Tell me what you want me to do."
She looked at him for a moment before answering.
